posts.author: Solar_Flare
posts.body:
Has anyone made a plugin that improves the pathfinding used when clicking on the map?
The only plugin I can find on the forums that does anything with pathfinding is Shaz's Smart Pathfinding plugin; but, as far as I can tell, all it does is makes events use the same pathfinding as touch movement. It doesn't alter how touch movement behaves in any way.
The following is a list of things I'd like to change about the pathfinding. It's just the things I've thought of and is probably not comprehensive. (Feel free to suggest other things if you think of them.)
Better pathing around obstacles. Currently, if you click on the other side of a wall, the player walks up to the wall and stops – even if there's a viable path around it.
Avoidance of damage terrain.
Prefer moving horizontally in sloped regions (eg when using Cae_SlopeMove).
Avoidance of events, or at least some types of events – map transfers in particular. Possibly others, I'd have to think on it more.
Contrarily, understanding of "teleporters" – events that transfer you to another point on the same map.
I'm thinking of creating such a plugin myself if it doesn't already exist, but I thought I may as well search and ask around first, just in case it has already been done.

posts.author: AquaEcho
posts.body:
Unfortunately pathfinding options in RPG Maker are severely lacking. They're pretty much all based on A* and I can't think of any that avoid events.
Your best options are Muki's plugin or the paid Rosedale collision plugin.
Better pathfinding is one of the reasons I picked up another engine (which has navmeshes, boids, the ability to mark any object as a pathfinding obstacle, etc).

posts.author: caethyril
posts.body:
Spoiler:
about A*
A* uses a heuristic to score any given node. The idea is to move from one node to the next until obtaining the best score, e.g. 0 (if using a "distance to goal" heuristic). Then you have a path!
A* is not the most efficient algorithm, but it is guaranteed to find a path if:
The heuristic is "perfect", e.g. it accurately predicts the distance to the goal.
This condition is met by default, but may break if using certain plugins.
And all available tiles are checked before giving up.
By default it searches only up to 12 tiles away.
The default search limit is aimed to work accurately and efficiently with the default screen size: 17x13 tiles. If you're using a larger screen size, or your maps are particularly complex, then failure can be expected.
In case it helps, here's an interactive demo to help visualise how A* works:
https://qiao.github.io/PathFinding.js/visual/
To emulate RPG Maker's default pathfinding, choose Heuristic: Manhattan and uncheck all Options. For further technical details, I generally recommend
this site
.
Like you've said, I think that realistically you'd need 1 big plugin for all the pathfinding stuff, since the core
findDirectionTo
is almost entirely just one big black box: it outsources the search limit, but basically nothing else.
Everything you've mentioned seems feasible~
Spoiler:
thoughts
Solar_Flare said:
Better pathing around obstacles. Currently, if you click on the other side of a wall, the player walks up to the wall and stops – even if there's a viable path around it.
Click to expand...
This might just be a matter of increasing the node search limit, e.g.
JavaScript:
/*:
 * @target MV MZ
 * @plugindesc Make pathfinding check further away before giving up.
 * @author Caethyril
 * @url https://forums.rpgmakerweb.com/threads/179951/
 * @help Free to use and/or modify for any project, no credit required.
 */
// Override - check up to 18 tiles away (default 12).
Game_CharacterBase.prototype.searchLimit = function() { return 18; };
Note that this would make all pathfinding potentially check 50% further away. Depending on map layout, this quadratically increases the number of tiles available for checking: it will be particularly noticeable on open-plan maps, much less so in narrow corridors.
Also, note that the search limit need not be sufficient to reach the goal, except in the most contrived situations. Typically it just needs to be enough to get you (heuristically)
nearer
to the goal.
Solar_Flare said:
Avoidance of damage terrain.
Click to expand...
"Avoidance" typically involves applying movement costs, e.g. make travelling over certain tiles, such as damage floors or specific regions, contribute more than 1 point of "distance travelled" to the heuristic, making it a less optimal path.
Solar_Flare said:
Prefer moving horizontally in sloped regions (eg when using Cae_SlopeMove).
Click to expand...
This could be done by changing the order of directional checks (e.g. <- -> ↑ ↓ instead of ↓ <- -> ↑) or with movement costs. Specific plugins/mechanics will likely need their own specific approaches.
Solar_Flare said:
Avoidance of events, or at least some types of events – map transfers in particular. Possibly others, I'd have to think on it more.
Click to expand...
Movement costs again, e.g. via event notetag.
Solar_Flare said:
Contrarily, understanding of "teleporters" – events that transfer you to another point on the same map.
Click to expand...
The pathfinding algorithm would have to have to be changed so it generates neighbouring tiles appropriately when situated appropriately relative to a "transfer" event. Feasible, but more complex if you want to accommodate other features like a moving entry/exit, randomised exit, etc.

posts.author: AquaEcho
posts.body:
The biggest problems with pathfinding in RPG Maker is massive lag, especially with multiple events pathfinding, getting stuck on walls all the time, and poor response to dynamic maps with moving events.
The pathfinding options all seem to go by the 48x48 tile grid for node calculations too. My research says some of these issues are inherent to A*.
I personally got tired of dealing with it in RPG Maker when other engines have multiple pathfinding options that let you adjust node granularity, give you far more control over the size and shape of collision masks of objects with WYSIWYG editors built directly into the engine, and simply work better straight out of the box.

posts.author: Solar_Flare
posts.body:
I'm not sure how you'd get massive lag if it's only used by touch movement… I could maybe see that happening if every moving event on the map was calling A* on every frame.
Which issues do you think are inherent to A*? Getting stuck on walls shouldn't be an issue of A*. I think A* probably isn't good at dealing with moving obstacles though.
I don't think collision masks have much to do with pathfinding at all…

posts.author: AquaEcho
posts.body:
Solar_Flare said:
I'm not sure how you'd get massive lag if it's only used by touch movement
Click to expand...
By default it's only used by touch movement but if you use Shaz, Muki, or other plugins to have events pathfind it lags. I am not the only one to experience this, especially when plugins like KOTC's pathfinder promise to reduce lag as a selling point (his one is buggy and crashes).
Lag, poor response to moving obstscles, and getting stuck (this is a function of not enough search length, but extending the length also increases lag) were cited as issues with A* in my research.
Custom collision masks are just another nice bonus feature other engines have that RPG Maker doesn't, when you have say, large enemies that take up more than 48x48 area that you want to pathfind or an unusual shape like a long car, in an environment made up of more than rigid 48x48 tile and event blocks.

If you have a twenty or thirty or a hundred events all pathfinding on every frame, I could maybe see it lagging. My use-case is primarily for touch movement though – I think there are few if any events that I'd want to use pathfinding for.
With moving obstacles, I think in many cases it's good enough to just ignore them – that is, treat their location as passable. They're going to move anyway, so by the time you actually get there, chances are they'll be gone. And if not, then there's a pretty good chance they'll move out of the way right after you get there.
And it seems you meant custom collision masks for the
agent

graphs

Solar_Flare said:
If you have a twenty or thirty or a hundred events all pathfinding on every frame, I could maybe see it lagging
Click to expand...
No it will lag even with only one event pathfinding if the search length is long enough. The issue compounds exponentially with every pathfinding event. It's noticable with only two or three.
I think you are narrowly focused on only your own use case of using pathfinding for only the player (one agent) when clicking to a location.
I am thinking bigger, with extremes like RTS gameplay where armies of units are pathfinding simultaneously.
Custom collision masks matter with the pathfinding agents, obstacles (e.g. other moving events) and environment, unless everything is comprised strictly of 48x48 blocks.

posts.author: Solar_Flare
posts.body:
Come to think of it, I wonder if one of the reasons the pathfinding lags so much if a lot of events are using it is because it
recalculates the path on every frame
. A* as an algorithm produces a complete path from one node to another, but
findDirectionTo
only grabs the first step in the path. Perhaps it would be faster if it cached the path for subsequent frames (as long as the goal point hasn't moved and something hasn't gone terribly wrong, like a step in the path turning out to be impossible once you get there).

posts.author: caethyril
posts.body: Generally RM will involve dynamic maps, so you may want to read up on D* (Lite). It determines a path up-front via A*, then recalculates blocked segments when appropriate.
